text:
Dylan Larkin will not be in Sunrise, and it has nothing to do with health. Detroit's longtime face has refused to play until he is traded, the team has him listed as suspended, and the Red Wings say they will not name a captain this season, per the Detroit Free Press. The trade talk is loud this week: reports have the Wild presenting the best offer and Montreal's Kent Hughes willing to meet Detroit's price. Until something happens, the Red Wings are playing in the shadow of it.

And the play has sagged. Detroit is winless in four, outscored 13-5, and the chances back that up: 43% of the expected goals in that run, the measure of who got the better looks. Moritz Seider's postgame frustration has become its own headline. John Gibson, who was 10.1 goals saved above expected last season, is at .866 and 6.1 below expected this year, .856 over his last five. Our playoff race gives Detroit a 20% chance. Viktor Arvidsson is pointless in four despite 3.3 expected goals in that stretch, which is the one piece of good news buried in the slump: the chances are there for him.

Florida is not whole either. Aleksander Barkov and Brad Marchand (both knee) are on injured reserve, with NHL.com reporting both could be back in about two weeks, and Sandis Vilmanis is out after the Tom Wilson hit that drew no supplemental discipline. Matthew Tkachuk has moved up beside Sam Reinhart and his brother Brady, and he has seven assists in a five-game point streak. Reinhart is two points from 700 for his career.

The special-teams matchup is the loudest number here. Florida's power play creates 1.17 expected goals a game, the Panthers take and draw more than five and a half penalties a night, and Detroit won the first meeting 5-3 on Nov. 2. Our numbers have Florida at 3.26 expected goals and Detroit at 3.00.
headline: Larkin's standoff hangs over a sliding Detroit
